接口参考

扩展可用的全部接口：视图协议、界面套件的类、面板块与表单字段、组件，以及宿主接口、应用对后端的调用、清单和实例类型描述的键，以及管理工具。内容由应用导出的接口定义生成。

本页逐项列出扩展可以使用的接口，每一项都有可以直接链接的锚点和简短示例。内容在构建本站时从应用仓库中提交的接口导出 sdk/interfaces/ 读取（由 bun run export:backend-interfaces 和 bun run export:frontend-interfaces 生成，过期时检查会失败），因此始终与应用的代码一致。各项的用法和语义见后端、实例类型和界面。

导出中的说明为英文

方法摘要、参数、权限、类和字段的说明直接取自导出，与应用代码中的注释相同，因此为英文。本页自身的文字为中文。

  • api 是后端协议的版本，即清单 engines.api 声明的版本。同一版本内只会增加方法和可选字段；删除或重命名会提升版本。
  • kitVersion 是界面套件的类 API 版本，规则相同。
  • uiApiVersion 是视图可用组件（组件包，UI API）的版本。同一版本内只会增加组件和可选属性；删除或重命名会提升版本。
  • exportVersion 是导出文件本身的格式版本。

前端

视图消息

视图页面与应用之间通过 postMessage 交换的消息。页面通常不直接发送这些消息，而是使用视图客户端，它封装了下面的全部消息。

Every message is an object with v (the protocol) and type.

页面 → 应用

open-settings

Opens a registered settings section through the host navigation. Returns null; an unknown section is invalid.

回答方: host

成员类型
idnumber | stringThe request's id, a finite number or non-empty text; its answer carries it.
sectionstringA currently registered settings section id; not a route.
open-external

Opens the URL in the system browser. Returns null; invalid URLs or opener failures reject the request. The frame never navigates the top-level window.

回答方: host

成员类型
idnumber | stringThe request's id, a finite number or non-empty text; its answer carries it.
urlstringAn HTTP or HTTPS URL, parsed once by Rust.
settings-get

Reads the frame owner's settings from the host, including for data-only extensions. Returns {values: Record<string, unknown>}; no extension id is accepted.

回答方: host

成员类型
idnumber | stringThe request's id, a finite number or non-empty text; its answer carries it.
settings-patch

Patches the frame owner's settings through the host's Rust validation and persistence. Returns {values: Record<string, unknown>}; no backend or extension id is required.

回答方: host

成员类型
idnumber | stringThe request's id, a finite number or non-empty text; its answer carries it.
patchRecord<string, unknown>Declared setting keys to change; null removes an override.
ready

The page is set up: the host sends theme and pings it from now on. Without it within 10 s the frame is unavailable.

成员: 无成员

call

Calls the extension's backend (ui.frame.call, within its 30 s bound); answered by result or error with the same id.

回答方: backend

成员类型
idnumber | stringThe request's id, a finite number or non-empty text; its answer carries it.
methodstringThe backend's method, non-empty.
params?unknownAny JSON; an absent one is null.
subscribe

The host hands the page the backend's events of that name for this frame.

成员类型
eventstringThe event's name, non-empty.
state

Reads the extension UI's state (ui.state, with the frame's context, within 10 s); answered by result (the state) or error. Without the hook ui it is unavailable.

回答方: backend

成员类型
idnumber | stringThe request's id, a finite number or non-empty text; its answer carries it.
subscribe-state

The host hands the page each state the extension's UI pushes from now on.

成员: 无成员

resize

The frame's height; there is no width, the frame spans its section. A frame shown as a page of its own ignores it.

成员类型
heightnumberThe page's height in CSS pixels, kept within 96–4096 (240 until the page sends one).
pong

The answer to ping.

成员: 无成员

focus-exit

Escape, unless the page prevented it: the host moves focus to what follows the frame, then takes the Escape as its own (in Settings, Settings closes).

成员: 无成员

pick-directory

Opens the application's folder dialog; result is the native path chosen, or null when cancelled.

回答方: host

成员类型
idnumber | stringThe request's id, a finite number or non-empty text; its answer carries it.
title?stringThe dialog's title, cut at 200 characters; anything but text is no title.
update-instance

In an instance's management section only, for the frame's own instance: the host asks the user to confirm the mode, then runs it with the recorded install values and values over them. result (null) once it has started; failed when the user declines, another update is waiting, or the application refuses it; invalid elsewhere.

回答方: host

成员类型
idnumber | stringThe request's id, a finite number or non-empty text; its answer carries it.
mode?"update" | "reinstall"Use update steps or reinstall in place. Defaults to update when available, otherwise reinstall.
valuesRecord<string, unknown>The install values to replace, at most 64.
navigate-instance

Takes the user to the instance's page (/instances/<instanceId>); result (null) once on its way, which may unmount the frame.

回答方: host

成员类型
idnumber | stringThe request's id, a finite number or non-empty text; its answer carries it.
instanceIdstringThe instance, non-empty.
open-management-section

Opens Instance Management at section, on instanceId or else on this frame's own instance, and returns null once it is on its way. Opening may unmount the frame.

回答方: host

成员类型
idnumber | stringThe request's id, a finite number or non-empty text; its answer carries it.
sectionstringA currently registered management section id; not a route. An unknown section is invalid.
instanceIdstring | nullThe instance whose management opens. Omitted: the instance this frame is in, which only a management.sections frame has.
open-dialog

Opens one of this extension's dialogs frames in a dialog over the window. result is what that page closed it with (close-dialog), or null when the user dismissed it; invalid for a frame that is not one of the extension's dialogs frames.

回答方: host

成员类型
idnumber | stringThe request's id, a finite number or non-empty text; its answer carries it.
framestringThe id of one of this extension's dialogs frames, non-empty.
title?stringThe dialog's title, cut at 200 characters; the frame's own when absent.
close-dialog

From a dialogs frame: closes its dialog and answers its opener with result. Ignored elsewhere.

成员类型
resultunknownWhat the opener's open-dialog resolves with, at most 65536 bytes as JSON; larger is null.
set-install-values

From a frame in the install wizard (install.frames): merges values into the install form's draft, as the user typed them, so the wizard's own validation and Rust's apply. result (null); invalid elsewhere.

回答方: host

成员类型
idnumber | stringThe request's id, a finite number or non-empty text; its answer carries it.
valuesRecord<string, unknown>Install values to merge into the wizard's draft, at most 64; keys the type's install form does not declare are dropped.
open-task-center-tab

Brings one of this extension's Task Center tabs forward, opening the Task Center if it is closed. result (null) once it is selected; invalid for a tab the application does not list for this extension.

回答方: host

成员类型
idnumber | stringThe request's id, a finite number or non-empty text; its answer carries it.
tabstringThe panel's or frame's own id in taskCenter.tabs; the application brings it forward.

ping

Every 5 s once the frame is ready; answered by pong. A frame that answers none for 12 s is unavailable.

One of this extension's Task Center tabs became the selected one: its page may refresh what it shows without polling.

成员类型
tabstringThe panel's or frame's own id.
theme

The application's theme and language, on ready and on every change of either.

成员类型

视图客户端

应用在每个扩展包根目录的保留路径提供的 ES 模块及其函数和类型。用法见界面。

__hanafubuki/frame.js · sdk/frame/frame.d.ts

ready

Tells the host the page is ready. Until it does, the host shows nothing; one that never does is unavailable after a few seconds. From then on the host sends the theme and the application's language, and follows the page's height. The client applies the theme to the page's root (data-theme, color-scheme and the tokens as CSS variables, which the UI kit __hanafubuki/ui.css reads) and the language to its lang.

返回: void

locale

The application's language (en, zh; the root's lang too), or null until the host has sent the theme, which it does once the page is ready.

返回: string | null

onLocale

Listens to the application's language: called when the host first sends it and on each change after; returns how to stop listening.

返回: () => void

call

Calls method of the extension's backend (ui.frame.call, within its 30 s bound) and resolves with what it answered; rejects with a FrameError. A data-only extension's frame has no backend: every call fails unavailable.

返回: Promise<T>

on

Listens to event, which the backend sends this frame (ui.frame.emit); returns how to stop listening.

返回: () => void

state

Reads the state of the extension's UI (ui.state, with the frame's context; within 10 s) and resolves with it; rejects with a FrameError. Only a backend that announces the hook ui has one: otherwise it fails unavailable.

返回: Promise<T>

getSettings

Reads this frame owner's settings; works without an extension backend.

返回: Promise<SettingsResult>

patchSettings

Patches this frame owner's declared settings through the host's validation and persistence. A null value removes that override. Returns all stored values after the write; works without an extension backend.

返回: Promise<SettingsResult>

onState

Listens to each state the extension's UI pushes (ui.emit, the last of those within 100 ms); returns how to stop listening. A push is the whole state, the same for every frame and panel of the extension. Read state once as well: a state pushed before the page listened is not sent again.

返回: () => void

pickDirectory

Opens the application's folder dialog, titled title (cut at 200 characters), and resolves with the native path the user chose, or null when they cancelled. The page is given the path alone: it cannot read the folder, and only its backend acts on it.

返回: Promise<string | null>

updateInstance

Updates or reinstalls the frame's instance after confirmation, with up to 64 install values replacing the recorded ones. When mode is omitted, a ready type with update steps is updated; other types reinstall in place. Rust validates the merged values. Resolves once it has started; its progress is the instance's install progress. Rejects with a FrameError of kind invalid outside an instance's management section, and failed when the user declines, another update is waiting for an answer, or the application refuses it.

返回: Promise<void>

navigateInstance

Takes the user to an instance's page (/instances/<instanceId>), as a downloader does after registering one; resolves once the application is on its way there, which may close the frame.

返回: Promise<void>

openSettings

Opens a currently registered settings section. Unknown sections reject with FrameError.

返回: Promise<void>

openManagementSection

Opens Instance Management at section — a currently registered management section id, not a route — for instanceId, or for the instance this frame is in when it is omitted. Resolves once the window is on its way, which may close the frame. An unknown section rejects with FrameError invalid, and so does a page outside instance management that names no instance.

返回: Promise<void>

openExternal

Opens an HTTP(S) URL in the system browser. Rust validates it; invalid URLs or opener failures reject.

返回: Promise<void>

openDialog

Opens one of this extension's dialogs frames (kind = "frame", slot = "dialogs") in a dialog over the window, titled title or by the frame's own title. Resolves with what that page's closeDialog gave, or null when the user dismissed it. Rejects invalid for a frame that is not one of the extension's dialogs frames, and failed while another dialog is open.

返回: Promise<T | null>

closeDialog

From a dialogs frame: closes its dialog, resolving the opener's openDialog with result (any JSON under 64 KiB). Ignored in any other frame.

返回: void

setInstallValues

From a frame in the install wizard ([[install.frames]] of an instance type): merges values into the install form's draft as if the user typed them, so the wizard's own validation and Rust's apply; keys the type's install form does not declare are dropped, at most 64 kept. Resolves once merged; rejects invalid elsewhere.

返回: Promise<void>

openTaskCenterTab

Brings one of this extension's Task Center tabs (taskCenter.tabs) forward by the panel's or frame's own id, opening the Task Center if it is closed. Resolves once it is selected; rejects invalid for a tab the application does not list for this extension.

返回: Promise<void>

onTaskCenterTabShown

From a Task Center tab's frame: called each time that tab becomes the shown one, tab its own id, so the page refreshes what it shows without polling; returns how to stop listening.

返回: () => void

FrameErrorKind

Why a call failed: the bridge's error type, or for state the extension UI's own (forbidden too). The host's own requests fail invalid (asked where they do not apply, or with members that do not read) or failed (the user declined, or the application refused).

FrameError

A call's failure, as call rejects with it.

SettingsResult

The extension's current stored setting overrides, validated by the host.

界面套件

__hanafubuki/ui.css 提供的类，按组列出，并给出修饰类、属性和示例标记。

Buttons

.btn

A button, 32px tall: a filled control with a slight raised edge, for every action that is not the primary one.

修饰类: .btn-primary, .btn-subtle, .btn-danger, .btn-icon, .btn-sm, .btn-lg

属性
disabledUnavailable.
aria-disabled="true"Unavailable but still focusable.
.btn-primary

The accent fill: the single most important action in a view, at most one.

修饰: .btn

.btn-subtle

No fill until hovered: toolbars, icon buttons, inline actions.

修饰: .btn

.btn-danger

Only the commit button of a destructive confirmation.

修饰: .btn

.btn-icon

A fixed square holding an icon; a size resizes the square, not its padding.

修饰: .btn

.btn-sm

24px: an action attached to one item of a dense list, a message or a row.

修饰: .btn

.btn-lg

40px: at most one hero call to action in a view.

修饰: .btn

Fields

.form-grid

Fields at least 360px wide, as many to a row as the form's width allows, one when it is narrow.

A field of a form-grid that needs the whole row.

Short inline help text for a field.

A checkbox and the words that name it, read as one line.

A group of content inside a page or panel, raised by its fill and stroke; never a shadow.

A sunken read-only region inside a card or panel: a list box, a readout, a log.

Anything laid over the content: a menu, a dropdown, a popover.

The content region beside a navigation pane.

                                                                                                                                                                                              AsyncRegion

                                                                                                                                                                                              A region whose content arrives: loading, then the content — or an empty state, or an error state that replaces a region that could not load. Moving between them is a state swap (spec §9.4): what the region holds fades out, then the next fades in, with no movement, so no caller chains LoadingState, EmptyState, and its content with v-ifs of its own (spec §7.17). A load that settles before LOADING_SHOW_DELAY_MS never showed its indicator, so the content simply appears: there was nothing on screen to swap out, and a fade would only delay it. The first render does not animate either. The caller decides the state; each one has a slot, and loading defaults to the shared LoadingState with loadingText. Where the shape of what arrives is known — rows, a card, a list of a usual length — the loading slot draws it at once in Skeletons instead, so the content lands in the room kept for it; the region is aria-busy meanwhile, since a stencil says nothing to a screen reader. The region lays its slot out as a column at its parent's gap, so wrapping content in it changes no spacing. A region sized by its content keeps its height through an animated swap and then travels to the new state's (size follow, spec §9.4), so what follows it glides instead of jumping when, say, a spinner gives way to a long list. A region that fills the room its parent gives it has nowhere to travel.

                                                                                                                                                                                              BaseCollapsible

                                                                                                                                                                                              A section that opens in place under its summary (spec §9.4, expand): a trigger that is the whole summary row, with the turning chevron at its end, and what it discloses beneath. The summary slot is the trigger's content and the default slot what it discloses, which stays mounted while closed, so a form inside it keeps its state. v-model is whether it is open; toggle says the user changed it. plain drops the well: the section is then a line of text that opens onto more text, which is what the conversation's own disclosures — a thinking block, a compaction — are. A box around each of them would read as a stack of widgets rather than as the transcript's prose.

                                                                                                                                                                                              BaseColorPicker

                                                                                                                                                                                              Colour picker primitive: a saturation/value field, a hue slider, and a hex field, all editing one #rrggbb value. Replaces <input type="color">, whose control is drawn by the platform. That meant a different dialog on every operating system, none of them themed, one of them a full-screen system panel — and on a frameless transparent window the native picker is the only thing on screen that does not belong to the app. This is the same interaction drawn from the app's own tokens, so it looks the same everywhere. Two events, deliberately. update:modelValue fires continuously so a preview can follow the drag; commit fires once the interaction settles. Anything that persists should listen to commit — a drag across the field is hundreds of intermediate colours, and writing each one would be hundreds of writes for a value the user has not chosen yet.

                                                                                                                                                                                              BaseColorPickerPopover

                                                                                                                                                                                              BaseColorPicker in a floating panel anchored to a trigger. Teleported to <body> and positioned in viewport coordinates, for the same reason BaseDropdown is: an absolutely positioned panel is laid out inside the nearest scrolling ancestor, so in a scrolling settings page it extends that region's scroll height. It never covered anything — it made the page taller, which reads as the layout stretching to accommodate it. Owning the panel here rather than in the caller is what makes the outside-click test correct too: once the panel is in <body> it is no longer inside the trigger's subtree, so a caller checking "did the click land in my element" would close the popover on every click *inside* it.

                                                                                                                                                                                              BaseDropdown

                                                                                                                                                                                              Dropdown with a rounded, animated menu. A native <select> popup is drawn by the operating system and cannot be given the radius, shadow, or open/close transition used by the app. This is a listbox the app draws itself, so it can. The cost of drawing it ourselves is that keyboard and screen-reader behaviour the native control gave for free has to be implemented, which is why this is a primitive rather than something a call site hand-rolls: role="listbox", arrow/Home/End/Enter/Escape, type-agnostic value contract, and focus returning to the trigger on close. The menu is teleported to <body> and positioned from the trigger's rect, the same approach Tooltip uses, because most call sites sit inside a panel that scrolls: an in-flow menu is clipped by the first ancestor with overflow, which for a settings field near the bottom of a panel means the options are simply not there. Scrolling or resizing closes it rather than chasing the trigger, which is roughly what a native select does too. It looks like a text field — the same box, with a chevron at its end — and, like one, draws the accent underline instead of a focus ring, both while it has focus and while its list is open. The list is a flyout (spec §7.10): the chosen option carries a check in its leading slot rather than a heavier weight, and the option under the keyboard cursor or the pointer takes the subtle hover fill. Presentation only: no i18n and no business logic. label names the control for assistive tech; placeholder is shown when nothing is selected. Inside a FormField or SettingsRow that names id, the field's visible words name the control in place of label, its hint, description, or error describes it, and an error marks it invalid.

                                                                                                                                                                                              BaseInput

                                                                                                                                                                                              Text/number input primitive. Wraps a native <input> with a single v-model contract so call sites stop hand-writing ($event.target as HTMLInputElement).value casts. Presentation only — validation and persistence stay in Rust. The component carries no i18n and no business logic; all native attributes (id, placeholder, min/max/step, aria-label, autocomplete, spellcheck) fall through to the input. type="number" emits number | null; other types emit string | null. With nullable, an empty value emits null instead of an empty string. ---- Committing ---- update:modelValue fires per keystroke and is only ever a draft. A call site that acts on the value — saving it, say — should listen to commit instead, which fires when the field is left or Enter is pressed, so the value it carries is one the user has finished typing. ---- Required fields ---- required is owned here rather than left to each call site, so every required field in the app signals the same way. An empty required field is marked invalid (aria-invalid, which the shared .text-input draws as a danger border and underline) once the user has left it, never while the form is still pristine — a form should not accuse the user before they have had a chance to fill it in. A caller that needs the state shown earlier (a rejected submit, say) can still force it with invalid, and a FormField showing an error forces it too. Inside a FormField or SettingsRow that names its id, the field's words name and describe the input (useFieldControl). ---- Stepping a number ---- type="number" replaces the platform spinner with the application's own arrows. The native one cannot be styled: its arrows are drawn inside a shadow element that takes a colour from the platform and paints its own pale box, and appearance: none removes the control rather than repainting it. So it is removed, and WinUI NumberBox's inline spin buttons are drawn in its place: two subtle 24px buttons side by side at the trailing end, inside the field. The buttons are hidden from assistive technology and skipped by the tab order, exactly as the platform spinner is. They duplicate what the input already does natively — Up and Down step the value while it has focus — so announcing them would offer a second route to the same thing rather than anything new.

                                                                                                                                                                                              BaseSelectableList

                                                                                                                                                                                              A list of mutually exclusive choices, where each row is too rich for a dropdown option but the choice is still one-of-many. ChoiceCard covers the same idea as a grid of cards for a handful of options; this covers a scrolling, filterable list of many. What it owns is the part that is easy to get wrong and tedious to repeat: radiogroup semantics, one tab stop for the whole list with arrow keys moving between rows, skipping disabled rows, and Home/End. The row's chrome — the shared RadioMarker and the subtle hover, pressed, and selected fills of a list row (spec §2.3) — is drawn here; what the row says is the caller's, through the item slot. Presentation only — no i18n. label names the group for assistive tech, and emptyText is shown when there is nothing to choose from.

                                                                                                                                                                                              BaseSlider

                                                                                                                                                                                              Drag-to-adjust slider for a bounded numeric setting. Drawn by the application rather than delegating to input[type=range]. A native range is rendered by the engine's shadow DOM, so its track geometry — and in particular how far the thumb travels — differs between the WebViews this app ships on. Owning the geometry is what makes the control identical everywhere, and it is why the thumb now reaches both ends. ---- Why the thumb reaches the ends ---- The thumb is a circle of width --slider-thumb, so its *centre* can only travel between thumb/2 and width - thumb/2 without the thumb hanging off the control. The bug this replaces came from mapping the pointer across the full width while drawing the thumb across that shorter travel: the two disagreed by half a thumb at each end, so the last sliver of the track was unreachable and the handle visibly stopped short of the end it was dragged to. Here one constant, travel, is both the rendering domain and the pointer-mapping domain, so pixel and value are exact inverses and min/max are reachable at — and only at — the ends of the rail. The fill is drawn to the thumb's centre. At max the thumb covers exactly the remaining half-thumb of rail, so the track reads as completely full. ---- Contract ---- update:modelValue fires continuously while dragging so the caller can show a live value; change fires once the value settles (pointer released, key pressed), which is the one a caller should persist on. Presentation only: no i18n and no business logic. label names the control for assistive tech, and formatValue supplies the spoken value.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Toggle switch primitive. Wraps a native <input type="checkbox" role="switch"> with a single boolean v-model contract, replacing the repeated <input type="checkbox" @change="x = ($event.target as HTMLInputElement).checked"> pattern and the ad-hoc .toggle-row checkbox styling. Presentation only — no i18n, no business logic. The native input keeps keyboard/focus semantics; the track and knob are decorative. Its name comes from the SettingsRow or FormField that names its id, or from an aria-label or aria-labelledby, which fall through to the input. Never wrap it in a <label>: only the switch itself toggles (spec §8.3).

                                                                                                                                                                                              BaseTabs

                                                                                                                                                                                              The shared tab list (spec §7.8, Fluent TabList): text tabs on whatever surface holds them, the selected one marked by an accent underline that slides between tabs. Presentation only. selectionMode="tabs" switches panels the caller owns (panelId links each tab to its panel); "radio" selects a persisted value with the same look. Either way the list is one tab stop with arrow keys, Home, and End inside it, and selection follows focus. Tabs are as wide as their labels and never wrap. When they do not fit, the ones that do not are folded into a MoreHorizontal menu; the selected tab is always kept on the strip. Arrow keys still walk every tab, folded or not: reaching a folded one selects it, which brings it onto the strip.

                                                                                                                                                                                              ContextMenu

                                                                                                                                                                                              The shared menu flyout (spec §7.10): a teleported, keyboard-accessible action list placed at a point — the pointer for a right-click, or just under a button that opens it. Presentation-only: the caller supplies already-translated labels and interprets the selected item id. Interaction contract. It opens with focus inside it: on its first item (or its last, for a menu opened with Up) when the control that opened it had keyboard focus, on the menu itself after a pointer press, as a native menu does. Arrow keys move between items and wrap, Home and End jump to the ends, and typing a letter moves to the next item that starts with it. Unavailable items stay reachable, so the reason they carry can be read, but do nothing. Enter or Space activates. It opens at the point and flips to the other side of it where the window has no room. Dismissal is the shared light dismissal (useLightDismiss): an outside press, Escape, Tab, the window losing focus, any scroll outside it, or a resize closes it, since its point no longer means anything. Closing, by dismissal or by choosing an item, hands focus back to the control that had it when the menu opened. Opening it again somewhere else while it is open — a right-click on another row — moves it there. That press closes the menu and the new one reopens it in the same tick, so open never drops; the new point arrives as new coordinates instead. The owner keeps it mounted and says whether it is open, rather than mounting it only while open: the menu emerges from its point as it opens and fades where it stands as it closes (popover-pop), and a component that is unmounted has no leave to play. While it fades it keeps the items and the point it was showing, and no longer takes the pointer.

                                                                                                                                                                                              CornerStatusStack

                                                                                                                                                                                              The status cards of one panel, docked to its bottom-end corner (spec §7.16): work the panel started, and how it ended. Each card is an overlay — the overlay fill, a surface stroke, the tooltip shadow — whose tone shows in its glyph and its edge, never in a wash over the whole card. The title says what, the detail line says how far or why, and a running operation carries its bar inside the card. An interactive entry's body opens where the work is reported in full (Task Center). A finished entry may take itself away after its lifetime; a failure never does. The countdown holds while the pointer is over the card or focus is inside it, so a card never vanishes while it is read or acted on. At most four cards show at once. More fold into a "+N more" row at the far end of the stack, which opens the whole stack until it is back to four. The cards nearest the corner stay — callers list the most current work last.

                                                                                                                                                                                              EmptyState

                                                                                                                                                                                              The "there is nothing here yet" state for a list container or a pane (spec §7.20). It is a component rather than a bare <p> because of where it goes: inside the container, filling it. Panels used to render the message *instead of* the box, so an empty list made the panel's lower half vanish and the layout jump — the box is part of the section's shape, not a wrapper the content earns by existing. It fills the box it is placed in and demands nothing of its own, so it can be dropped into a flex row, a flex column, a grid area, or a plain block without the container arranging anything around it. It has no height of its own to offer, either: a container that sizes to its content states its own floor, because that container is the box a user sees and the floor is that box's shape, not the message's. Inside that box the message is a centred column, at most 360px wide. A pane-sized state — one with a glyph or a title — starts --space-10 from the top; a text-only message, which is what a list card shows, starts --space-6 down so it does not sit low in a short box. Presentation-only and i18n-free: callers pass already-translated text. On its own, text is the whole message. A larger empty surface — a pane or a library with nothing in it yet — can add a 32px icon and a title; text is then the description beneath the title, saying what to do about it. The #action slot takes at most one button: a default .btn, or a primary one only when it is the single way forward. The same layout is the error state: tone="danger" draws the glyph in the danger colour (a CircleX unless the caller names another), the title says what failed, text carries the reason, and the action is the way forward — usually Retry.

                                                                                                                                                                                              FormField

                                                                                                                                                                                              The shared label / help / error scaffold for a single form control. It folds together the near-identical .field + <label> + help + error markup that settings fields and manage-panel fields each used to hand-roll, so every field reads the same and long-form guidance collapses into one InfoTooltip beside the label. Presentation-only and i18n-free: pass already-translated strings. The control goes in the default slot, which receives the resolved controlId to give it; pass an explicit controlId when the caller owns the id. #label-suffix adds trailing label content such as an ownership pill; help is the collapsed tooltip; hint is brief inline guidance under the control; error replaces the hint when present. The label names the control and the line under it describes it: the input primitives read useFieldControl, which links the label text through aria-labelledby, the line through aria-describedby, and, for an error, marks the control aria-invalid — which is also what turns the field's border and underline to the danger colour. The label is text, not a <label>, so clicking it does nothing (spec §8.3). The error carries an icon as well as its colour, so it never rests on colour alone.

                                                                                                                                                                                              InfoBar

                                                                                                                                                                                              An inline message about a page, panel, or form: something failed, needs attention, or is worth knowing (spec §7.15, WinUI InfoBar, Fluent MessageBar). Field-level problems belong to FormField, and the progress or outcome of an operation belongs to its status card; this is the message that sits in the content itself. It is tinted with its severity and carries the matching glyph, so the severity never rests on colour alone. The title and message read as one wrapping paragraph and are never truncated — an error is read in full. Text stays primary; only the glyph takes the status colour (spec §2.6). Errors and warnings interrupt (role="alert"); success and information wait their turn (role="status"). Nothing here times out: a message stays until its condition clears — the caller's v-if — or the user dismisses it. An error or warning should offer the way out in the #action slot (Retry, Open settings) whenever there is one; the slot takes one small default button. Presentation-only and i18n-free: the caller passes translated text, and a dismissLabel — present, it adds the subtle dismiss button that names it. It opens and closes with expand, so the content around it moves aside rather than jumping, the bar's margins and the gap beside it included (expandGapHooks). A bar that is already there when its page first renders arrives with the page and does not animate; one that appears later does. It comes and goes only through open: a caller's v-if would unmount the bar's own transition with it, so the bar would vanish instead of collapsing (check:frontend rejects one). A caller's class and attributes land on the bar's region, so they leave with it rather than staying on the transition.

                                                                                                                                                                                              LoadMoreSentinel

                                                                                                                                                                                              The trailing row of a list revealed in batches (useIncrementalReveal): when it nears the viewport the next batch loads, and until then it says so. Render it last in the list, only while there is more to show, and give it the list's sentinel ref — the composable reads this row's element from it. It is a list item, so it belongs inside the <ul>/<ol> with the rows it trails. It draws no divider of its own. A list whose rows are ruled gives this row its rule through a class, the same as any other row; a list of spaced cards leaves it plain. Presentation-only and i18n-free: the caller passes the translated label. It is hidden from assistive technology, which reaches the next batch by reading on, not by being told one is loading.

                                                                                                                                                                                              LoadingState

                                                                                                                                                                                              A centered spinner and label for a content area that is still loading (spec §7.17). A spinner means the region is blocked; non-blocking work reports through a progress bar instead. Anti-flash: a wait shorter than LOADING_SHOW_DELAY_MS shows nothing, so quick work never flashes an indicator. The region itself renders at once and keeps its size throughout, so the layout does not shift when the spinner arrives — only the spinner and label wait. There is deliberately no minimum time on screen once it shows (spec §7.17). The swap from it to whatever replaces it — content, an empty state, an error state — is AsyncRegion's, which callers wrap their regions in rather than removing this with a v-if of their own. Presentation-only and i18n-free: the caller passes an already-translated text, a short "-ing…" phrase such as "Loading instances…". role="status" + aria-live="polite" announces the label when it appears; the region is present from the start so the announcement is heard. Under reduced motion the spinner stands still and the label carries the state.

                                                                                                                                                                                              NavList

                                                                                                                                                                                              The navigation and master list of spec §7.9: settings navigation, the manage rail, the instance list, the Task Center list, and the conversation list are all this one pattern. It owns what every one of those lists must get the same: the row backplate and its hover, pressed, and current fills; the selection pill; one tab stop with arrow keys inside the list; and the ARIA that says what "current" means. What a row *says* is the caller's — the default row is an icon and a label, and a rich row (an instance with its status, a task with its progress) replaces it through the default slot. semantics is the one real difference between the five lists: navigation the item is where you are (aria-current="page"); rows may carry their own action buttons beside the item selection the item is the chosen row of a master/detail pair (listbox/option, aria-selected); options cannot contain controls, so these rows carry no actions and activation is the keyboard's: focus moves the current item with the arrow keys, for lists whose content is cheap to show; manual only moves focus, and Enter or Space opens the item, for lists whose items open heavy content. Rows that come and go open and close in place (spec §9.4, list row): each row is an expand region of a TransitionGroup, so the rows after it follow it and no consumer wraps its rows. A row is also a .reveal-host, so a control in its actions slot can be a .hover-reveal.

                                                                                                                                                                                              PathInput

                                                                                                                                                                                              A path typed or picked: a text input with a Browse button beside it that opens the host's dialog (its PathPicker). The dialog starts at whatever the field already holds, so browsing from a filled-in path begins next to it. A pick replaces the value and also emits picked: a path from the dialog is always complete, so a caller that saves only on commit (the end of typing) can save a pick straight away. Everything else given to the component — id, placeholder, required, nullable, a commit listener — goes to the input; class and style go to the row, for the caller's layout. The button stays beside the input at every width: it is a single icon, so stacking it under the input would only cost a row. Paths are set in the monospace face, where a slash, a dot, and a similar-looking name are easiest to tell apart.

                                                                                                                                                                                              ProgressBar

                                                                                                                                                                                              The one progress bar: a track and its fill, for every surface that reports how far along something is. value is a percentage. null means the amount is unknown, and the fill becomes the shared sweep rather than claiming a number nobody has; the bar then drops aria-valuenow, which is how assistive technology tells an indeterminate bar from an empty one. Its look is the shared .progress-bar (primitives.css, which the frame UI kit carries too); the component adds the value, its bounds, and the ARIA. It draws the bar only. Where it sits — its flex basis, minimum width, margins — belongs to the caller through a class on the component, and so does any percentage or count printed beside it, because every surface lays those out differently. The shared class therefore sets no layout property a caller would, so one never has to win over the other.

                                                                                                                                                                                              RadioMarker

                                                                                                                                                                                              The one radio glyph (spec §7.5): a 20px ring that fills with the accent and shows a dot when checked. ChoiceCard and BaseSelectableList both draw it, so the two radio choices in the app cannot drift apart again. It is decoration, never the control. The element that carries role="radio" and aria-checked owns the semantics, the hit target, and focus; this only mirrors its state. That parent is also what the pointer is over, so the dot follows *its* hover and press — 12 at rest, 14 on hover, 10 while pressed (WinUI RadioButton) — through the [role="radio"] ancestor selector below rather than through props a caller would have to keep in step with the pointer.

                                                                                                                                                                                              RefreshButton

                                                                                                                                                                                              A refresh action whose own icon spins while the refresh is in flight, so progress is shown in place. It replaces the pattern of a plain button paired with a separate "refreshing…" status note in the panel header — that note appeared and disappeared on every refresh and shifted the surrounding layout. The button keeps a constant size (the label never changes), so nothing jumps. Presentation-only and i18n-free: the caller passes an already-translated label, which is the visible text and the accessible name. busy drives the spin and disables the control to prevent overlapping refreshes; disabled covers other reasons the action is unavailable (e.g. an initial load). Labelled, it is a default button beside a panel's other actions. Icon-only, it is a subtle square (btn-subtle btn-icon), the shape every toolbar icon button takes (spec §7.1), so a caller does not restate those classes.

                                                                                                                                                                                              A run of related SettingsRows (spec §7.21): the rows stack 4 apart, under an optional Body Strong group header 8 above them. A panel's own PanelHeader already names a group that is the whole panel, so such a group leaves title out. Groups on one page sit 24 apart; that is the page's gap, since a group sets no margin of its own. The run is the shared .card-list (primitives.css), as each row is a .card-row.

                                                                                                                                                                                              SettingsRow

                                                                                                                                                                                              One setting, laid out as a Windows 11 Settings row (spec §7.21): a card at least 64 tall with an optional 20px leading icon, the setting's name in Body and what it does in a secondary Caption beneath it, and the control at the trailing end. Related rows stack 4 apart inside a SettingsGroup. Settings' pages are built from it, and an extension's Settings section may be (the frame component bundle). Its narrow layout answers a container named panel, which the page it is on declares. - controlId names the control the row is about: the input primitives inside it with that id take the title as their name and the description as their description (useFieldControl). The title is text, not a <label>, so clicking it does nothing: only the control's own box opens, toggles, or focuses it (spec §8.3). - stacked puts the control under the text at the row's full width, for a control that needs the room (a path, a list). Every row stacks this way once its panel is narrower than 480. - nested indents the row's content by 48 under the row above it, for a setting that only means something while its parent is on (spec §5.1). - The title slot replaces the title text, for a row whose name is still being read: a Skeleton there keeps the row its final height. The title greys with a disabled field or switch, so the pair reads as one setting that is unavailable; the description keeps its colour, because for an unavailable setting it is where the reason goes. Presentation-only and i18n-free: callers pass translated text.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Skeleton

                                                                                                                                                                                              A placeholder holding the place of content that has not arrived yet, at the size that content will take (spec §7.17): Fluent's Skeleton — a neutral grey stencil, --fill-track, with a lighter wave crossing it on the shared shimmer loop (spec §9.6). Two card fills, as an earlier placeholder swept between, are too close to tell apart, so loading read as empty. A view draws its own structure at once — headers, labels, rows — and puts a skeleton where each read value goes, so the value lands in the place kept for it and nothing around it moves. - text stands in for a run of text: it is one line of the surrounding type tall, so whatever holds it is exactly as tall as it will be with its text. - control stands in for a field or a button: a control's height. - block is sized entirely by the caller (a tile, an image). width and height size it to what it stands in for (any CSS length or token), so it is as large as that content and nothing moves when the content replaces it; it never grows past its container. Text takes only a width: its height is the line's. It is decorative: the region that is loading says so (aria-busy), not each stencil.

                                                                                                                                                                                              StatusBadge

                                                                                                                                                                                              The one status badge: a short label for a state — running, installed, update available, restart required (spec §7.19). It is Fluent 2's Badge in its medium size, rounded shape, and tint appearance: 20 tall with the in-page 4px corner rather than a pill, filled with its tone's tint, edged with its border, and lettered in its foreground. A badge is short, so its label takes the status colour rather than primary text. info and accent both read in the accent; neutral is the plain grey wash with a neutral stroke and secondary text. dot adds a leading 6px dot (Fluent's tiny badge), so the state does not rest on colour alone. pulse makes that dot breathe, for a state that is still in progress (starting, installing, checking); it implies the dot. Under reduced motion the dot simply stays lit. A caller that marks the state with a glyph instead puts a 12px icon in the slot before the label. Presentation-only: the caller supplies the translated label and decides the tone. A tone of undefined is neutral, so a mapping can leave a state unmarked by returning nothing. Attributes such as role="status" pass through to the pill.

                                                                                                                                                                                              ToolbarSlot

                                                                                                                                                                                              One control in a row of controls that is only sometimes there. Wrapping a conditional control here, instead of giving it a bare v-if, makes it come and go with the shared toolbar-slot transition in base.css: the row opens a gap and the control rises into it, or the control retracts upward and the row closes over the gap. The row's other controls never jump. The control shows while when is truthy, and the slot receives that value narrowed, so a control that reads from a nullable value names it once: <ToolbarSlot :when="context.primaryAction" #default="{ value: action }"> Attributes land on the slot element, which is the row's flex item; the row owns its layout (shrinking, ordering) through a class passed here. A row with a gap also declares it as --toolbar-slot-gap, so a closed slot gives that gap back. Nothing animates on the first render: a control that was already there when the row appeared did not arrive. A control that becomes a different control in the same place — Launch becomes Stop — names which one it is in swapKey: a new key is a new control, so the old one leaves its slot as the new one arrives in its own (spec §9.4, keyed by identity), rather than changing its label and width in place.

                                                                                                                                                                                              TokenListInput

                                                                                                                                                                                              A list of short strings the user builds: one entry per row, added with the field under them and taken out one at a time. The settings that hold one are lists of names, not prose — the Agent plugins turned off, the engines a search pool draws on — so a textarea whose lines are the entries makes a one-line edit read as a paragraph break, hides how many entries there are, and offers no way to remove one without counting lines. The entries are the same array a textarea's lines were: the value is the strings, unchanged. Presentation only: the caller owns the array and Rust validates it. The list's own bounds, where it has them, are what stop an entry being added or a longer one being typed; a blank entry or one already in the list is not added, because neither is a new entry.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Tooltip

                                                                                                                                                                                              Presentation-only tooltip primitive. The default slot is the trigger; the text prop (or the content slot) is the floating description shown on pointer rest and keyboard focus. The popover is teleported to <body> and positioned with position: fixed from the trigger's rect, so it is never clipped by a panel's overflow scroll container. Use this where the description is richer than a line of text, or where the trigger exists only to carry it (InfoTooltip). An ordinary control that describes itself needs nothing here: a title attribute is taken over by nativeTooltips and drawn as the same bubble, on the same clock (tooltipTiming) — the show and hide delays, the warm hand-off between tooltips, and the instant dismissal on Escape, a press, scrolling, or a resize all come from there. Focus a script restores, or a click gives, shows nothing; only keyboard focus does. Losing focus hides it at once. Accessibility: the trigger is described by the popover through aria-describedby; the popover carries role="tooltip" and is never interactive. This component adds no business logic and owns no state beyond open/position.

                                                                                                                                                                                              The floating bubble every tooltip in the application is drawn as.                                                                                                                                                                                               UpdateDot

                                                                                                                                                                                              "An update is available" marker: a solid dot with two rings pulsing outward from its centre, which is what makes the marker readable in peripheral vision — a static dot of this size is easy to miss in a list of rows. The waves are spaced rather than continuous: the marker sits in a persistent surface, so a ripple that never rests reads as agitation instead of a notice. The rings are pseudo-elements taken out of flow, so the marker occupies exactly the dot's own box and animating it never reflows the row around it. Presentation only. The caller supplies the accessible treatment it needs — a title for the hover description, aria-hidden where a neighbouring label already carries the meaning — and those attributes fall through to the root.

                                                                                                                                                                                                Permissions
                                                                                                                                                                                                • filesystemFilesystemAccess可选Schema 默认 "extension-data"

                                                                                                                                                                                                  Where the extension's processes may run.

                                                                                                                                                                                                  FilesystemAccess

                                                                                                                                                                                                    以下之一:

                                                                                                                                                                                                    "extension-data"

                                                                                                                                                                                                    Its own data directory.

                                                                                                                                                                                                    "own-instances"

                                                                                                                                                                                                    Its own data directory and the directories of its own types' instances.

                                                                                                                                                                                                  • instancesInstancesAccess可选Schema 默认 "none"

                                                                                                                                                                                                    Which instances the extension may read.

                                                                                                                                                                                                    InstancesAccess

                                                                                                                                                                                                      以下之一:

                                                                                                                                                                                                      "none"
                                                                                                                                                                                                      "read"

                                                                                                                                                                                                      Every instance, read only (instances.list, instances.get).

                                                                                                                                                                                                      "own-types"

                                                                                                                                                                                                      The instances of its own types (instances.ofType, servers.status); with registerInstances, instances.import of its own types.

                                                                                                                                                                                                      "all"

                                                                                                                                                                                                      Both; with registerInstances, instances.import of any type.

                                                                                                                                                                                                    • managementManagementAccess可选Schema 默认 "none"

                                                                                                                                                                                                      The management catalog's tools.

                                                                                                                                                                                                      ManagementAccess

                                                                                                                                                                                                        以下之一:

                                                                                                                                                                                                        "none"
                                                                                                                                                                                                        "read"

                                                                                                                                                                                                        The read tools.

                                                                                                                                                                                                        "confirm"

                                                                                                                                                                                                        Every tool; each mutation runs only once the user confirms it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                      • networkstring[]可选Schema 默认 []

                                                                                                                                                                                                        Hosts download.fetch, git.clone and git.pull may reach: a name, or *. and a suffix.

                                                                                                                                                                                                      • processesboolean可选Schema 默认 false
                                                                                                                                                                                                      • registerInstancesboolean可选Schema 默认 false

                                                                                                                                                                                                        instances.scan and instances.import: it may add instances.

                                                                                                                                                                                                    • protocolVersioninteger可选Schema 默认 0

                                                                                                                                                                                                      minimum: 0

                                                                                                                                                                                                    事件主题

                                                                                                                                                                                                    events.subscribe 替换订阅。每条 event 通知包含 topic 及承载下方结构的 data。结构来自协议 topic registry；preferences 与 host.preferences 使用同一完整快照，settings 仍只表示扩展自身设置。启动或重新订阅时主动读取当前偏好；通知不重放。

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  管理工具

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  后端用 tools.list 列出管理目录工具，用 tools.call 调用。下表中的 read 表示只读工具，修改操作需要 management = "confirm" 并由用户在主窗口逐次确认。标为“仅内置实例”的工具会拒绝扩展提供的实例类型。启动任务的工具返回 activityId，后端可订阅 task 事件跟踪进度。见后端。

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  按操作对象选择工具。例如，install_extension 给指定 WebUI 实例安装插件；list_host_extensions 列出 Hanafubuki 本身已安装的扩展，browse_host_extension_marketplace 查询桌面扩展市场。用户在设置中确认桌面扩展的安装。
